description:
Retype issue ids in the CLI integration tests that drive the library directly.

## Background

Integration suites link the library with the `test-support` feature (`crates/jit/Cargo.toml:103`), so the shared canonical-id fixture in `jit::test_utils` is reachable. Their helpers take and return ids as `&str` or `String`, and assertions compare ids and dependency lists with strings; once ids are validated, those comparisons and conversions stop compiling. Hierarchy vector node ids model graph nodes, not issues. Most `cli_*` tests drive the binary and exchange ids as process strings, which is the CLI boundary. The files in the footprint also call executor or storage APIs directly.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Library-facing code in the listed `cli_*` files takes and returns issue ids as `IssueId` and uses no non-UUID issue id.
- [hard] REQ-02: Ids exchanged with the binary stay strings at the process boundary, parsed once where a test hands them to the library.
- [hard] REQ-03: Suite helpers take `&IssueId` and pass `&IssueId` onward, so callees that still take `&str` accept them through deref coercion.
- [hard] REQ-04: Code in this family, its unit-test modules included, uses issue ids only through `as_str()`, `short_id()`, `Display`, `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`/`Eq`, `PartialOrd`/`Ord`, `Hash` and serde, so it compiles unchanged once `IssueId` is the validated newtype.

## Notes

`crate::domain::identity::IssueId` is at this point an alias for `String`, and the `IssueIdStaging` trait gives it `short_id()`. Retyping to the alias is compiler-neutral, so this change is checked by its criteria rather than by type errors; a later change replaces the alias with the validated newtype and the compiler then reports any site missed here. Parameters are retyped outside-in: the CLI and server entry points already resolve ids, and callers in this family are retyped before the functions they call in inner layers.
title: CLI suites that use the library carry typed issue ids
